writeup.headline: Fortrea rates Sell by a single point: strong share price momentum against shrinking revenue and thin margins.
writeup.thesis: Fortrea scores 44, one point below the Hold band, as weak fundamentals outweigh an exceptional price trend. Growth scores 22, with a TTM revenue decline of 2.1%, a latest-quarter revenue decline of 4.5% year on year, and growth slowed by 2.2 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (33) and balance sheet (28) are also weak: operating margin is -0.4%, FCF margin excluding prepayments is 2.8% (7.3% reported), diluted share count up 4.6% year on year, and net debt is 4.52 times FCF with cash covering only 0.16 of debt. Valuation scores 32; P/S of 0.9x is low in absolute terms, but P/FCF is 32.5x on FCF excluding prepayments, EBIT is negative, and the FCF yield sits 1.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, while the stock is expensive against its own history on P/S (more expensive than at 30 of the last 32 month-ends). Offsetting this, trend scores 100, with the price at its 52-week high and shares up 90.0% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, and news is mildly positive (61) after a Q3 beat and raised guidance midpoints.
key_risks: Revenue keeps shrinking, with a latest-quarter revenue decline of 4.5% year on year and $558 million of backlog removed for inactive trials.
Cash flow leans on customer prepayments: contract liabilities rose $120.3M, and FCF excluding them gives a much thinner 2.8% margin.
Leverage is meaningful, with net debt at 4.52 times FCF and cash to debt of 0.16.
After a run to its 52-week high, 65.4% above its 200-day average, the shares are exposed to a sharp pullback if momentum fades.
Ongoing dilution, with diluted share count up 4.6% year on year.
what_would_change: Just 1 more point would lift the score to Hold (45), for example from revenue returning to growth or the guidance raise showing up in a better growth score.
Sustained positive operating margin and higher free cash flow excluding prepayments would lift quality, balance sheet and valuation scores.
A fall to Strong Sell needs a 15-point drop below 30, most plausibly from the trend score unwinding from 100 alongside further revenue declines or negative news.
